id: ml-11
title: BERT
paper: Devlin et al., BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding (arXiv Oct 2018; NAACL 2019)
link: https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.04805
type: Replication
cutoff: 2018-10-11
domain: ml
profile: method-benchmark

## expected_verdict
Supported (scoped), with a component-level refutation. Masked-LM pretraining gains are confirmed and exceeded by RoBERTa's replication, which also finds BERT "significantly undertrained". The paper's ablation claim that next-sentence prediction (NSP) helps is not supported: under a better-controlled input format, removing NSP matches or slightly improves downstream results.

## I0
Does masked-language pretraining improve downstream language tasks, and does sentence prediction help?

## evidence
- Pretraining: masked LM + NSP on BooksCorpus (800M words) + English Wikipedia (2,500M words); BERT-Base and BERT-Large.
- Results: GLUE score 80.5 (+7.7 points), SQuAD v1.1 test F1 93.2 (+1.5), SQuAD v2.0 test F1 83.1 (Abstract).
- NSP ablation (Table 5, BERT-Base dev): with NSP vs No NSP: MNLI-m 84.4 vs 83.9; QNLI 88.4 vs 84.9; MRPC 86.7 vs 86.5; SST-2 92.7 vs 92.6; SQuAD F1 88.5 vs 87.9. Authors conclude removing NSP hurts, notably on QNLI and SQuAD.
- NSP is trivially easy (97–98% accuracy).
- Model size: larger models improve all tasks (Table 6, 5 fine-tuning restarts).

## intake
- Scope: (A) bidirectional masked-LM pretraining improves downstream NLU; (B) the NSP objective contributes to that gain.
- Regime: GLUE, SQuAD, SWAG; BERT-Base/Large; a fixed pretraining budget and input format.
- Assumptions for (B): the No-NSP ablation changes only the objective; input format, sequence length and training tokens held equal.
- Falsifiers: for (B), removing NSP with a matched input format and token budget does not hurt; for (A), gains vanish against equally trained left-to-right LMs.

## screen
- Must flag: the NSP ablation also changes the input construction (segment pairs); single training run per ablation; possible under-training of all variants.
- Must request: NSP ablation with matched input format and data/tokens; multiple seeds.

## retrieval
- Pre-cutoff must-finds: ELMo (Peters et al. 2018); OpenAI GPT (Radford et al. 2018); ULMFiT; Transformer (Vaswani et al. 2017); GLUE (Wang et al. 2018); cloze / skip-thought objectives.
- Current mode: Liu et al. 2019, RoBERTa: replication finds BERT significantly undertrained; training longer, larger batches, more data (160GB), dynamic masking, and removing NSP (DOC-SENTENCES / FULL-SENTENCES formats) matches or slightly improves downstream performance; GLUE 88.5.

## designer
- Ablate NSP with identical input format (full sentences across documents), same tokens and steps; evaluate GLUE/SQuAD over ≥ 3 fine-tuning seeds.

## champion
- MLM-only model with FULL-SENTENCES or DOC-SENTENCES input at matched tokens (RoBERTa's control).

## panel
- Accept (A); flag (B) as confounded by input format; request the matched ablation.

## run
- Small-scale: pretrain a mini-BERT with and without NSP (matched format) on a Wikipedia subset; compare MNLI/QNLI. Full replication is GPU-weeks (BLOCKED locally).

## verdict
- Label: Supported (scoped) for pretraining gains; NSP contribution not supported.
- Must say: gains replicated and improved with longer training; NSP helps only under the original confounded ablation.
- Must not say: BERT's gains were illusory; or NSP is essential.

## audit
- Check: 80.5 / 93.2 / 83.1; Table 5 rows; RoBERTa "significantly undertrained", 160GB, NSP removal result, GLUE 88.5.

## variants
- Objective changes (MLM variants, sentence-order prediction) under matched token budgets.
